references.text: The basic law concerning the tithe: every tenth part of the land, whether from the produce of the soil or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord and is holy to him.
The Levites shall receive the tithe as their inheritance in return for their service at the tent of meeting.
The Levites must give a tenth part of the tithe they receive.
The tithe shall be brought to the place the Lord chooses, along with other offerings and gifts.
Prohibition against eating the tithe of grain, wine, and oil within the city gates.
Every third year, the tithe is to be given to Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
The people gave generously from the firstfruits and the tithe when Hezekiah reformed the worship.
The people committed themselves to bringing the tithe of the produce of the land to the Levites.
All Judah brought the tithe of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.
The prophet Malachi rebukes the people for withholding the tithe and urges them to bring the full tithe into the storehouse.
Jesus mentions the Pharisees' precise practice of tithing but points out that they neglect more important matters such as justice, mercy, and faithfulness.
Jesus criticizes the Pharisees for tithing on herbs while neglecting justice and love for God.
The Pharisee in the parable boasts that he gives a tenth of all he earns.
